answer_text:
# Train Passing a Bridge Problem

## Setting Up the Problem

When a train **completely passes** a bridge, the total distance traveled equals:

$$\text{Total distance} = \text{Length of bridge} + \text{Length of train}$$

## Calculating

**Total distance covered:**
$$d = 650 + 200 = 850 \text{ meters}$$

**Speed of the train:**
$$v = \frac{d}{t} = \frac{850}{17} = 50 \text{ meters per second}$$

## Verification

- Distance: 650 m (bridge) + 200 m (train) = 850 m ✓
- Time at 50 m/s: 850 ÷ 50 = 17 seconds ✓

All values are consistent.

$$\boxed{50}$$
